# i2c-scanner

<!-- Generated by tools/build-user-docs.py; edit tools/sketch-guides.json. -->

**Level:** Sensors. No AI subscription or API key is needed.

[Start here](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html) · [Website instructions](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/sketches.html#i2c-scanner) · [All sketches](../README.md)

## What you should see

The serial monitor lists addresses on the SDA/SCL header bus every five seconds. With no devices, an empty scan is expected. The matrix is not used.

## What you need

No components needed for an empty scan. Optional: a compatible I2C device on the SDA/SCL header pins with common GND and its required supply. Power down before wiring. Qwiic uses a separate bus; read the limitation below.

Install Arduino_RouterBridge with Library Manager. The UNO Q core supplies the board-specific headers.

## Upload this sketch

1. Complete the getting-started guide once to install the UNO Q core and libraries.
2. In Arduino IDE, open i2c-scanner/i2c-scanner.ino. Select Arduino UNO Q and its port.
3. Click Verify, then Upload. Uploading replaces the running microcontroller sketch.

Or, in the **UNO Q Linux terminal**, from the repository root:

```bash
python3 flash i2c-scanner
```

Read the replacement prompt and enter `y` to compile and upload. To check compilation without uploading:

```bash
python3 flash i2c-scanner --compile-only
```

The helper uploads locally on the board. For a computer-side IDE or network CLI upload, follow the getting-started guide.

## Try it

Try the empty-bus scan first. Then power down, attach a compatible I2C device on the header bus, and compare the next scan after powering up.

This sketch has no serial command controls. To change its behavior, edit the source, save, compile, and upload again.

## Limits and tips

This sketch calls Wire.begin(), Wire.beginTransmission(), and Wire.endTransmission(). Current Arduino documentation assigns the Qwiic connector to Wire1. For a Qwiic experiment, replace those three Wire calls with Wire1, then Verify and Upload; that variant has not been compiled or hardware-tested here. The original header comment describing Qwiic scanning is too broad. Device-name annotations are guesses based on addresses, not positive identification.

## If it does not work

Compare the result with the expected behavior above, then follow [troubleshooting](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#troubleshooting). Save your edits before downloading or uploading another version.

The repository records compilation with UNO Q core 0.56.0 on the original board. Typed serial input and most visual behavior still need hardware verification. These instructions describe the source code, not a new hardware test.

[Read the source](i2c-scanner.ino) for the implementation and its original compile/upload commands.
